title: Exam Technique and Final Review

header.html: exam strategy and review of every objective
the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

toc.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse

html:
1Time plan

Maximum of 90 questions in 90 minutes: about one minute per question, with the performance-based questions (PBQs) taking more. [Verify live] for the final V8 numbers.

Pass What to do Time
First pass Answer quick questions; flag PBQs and doubtful ones About 50 minutes
PBQs Do them after the quick questions: read the whole task, do what you can, never leave one blank About 25 minutes
Final pass Review flagged questions; make sure every question has an answer About 15 minutes

2The routine for every question

  1. Read the last sentence first: what is asked?
  2. Mark the key words: BEST, FIRST, MOST likely, LEAST, NOT, EXCEPT.
  3. Name the domain and objective (control, threat, architecture, operations, governance).
  4. Remove options from the wrong category.
  5. Choose the answer that fits the constraint in the scenario (cost, time, law, availability).
  6. Choose-two/three questions: select exactly the number asked.
Exam tip

. CompTIA often offers two plausible answers. The better one fits the exact scenario, the stated constraint and the question word (first step, best control, most cost-effective).

3Domain checklists

1.0 General Security Concepts (16%)

  • CIA, AAA, non-repudiation, Zero Trust, least privilege, defense in depth
  • Control categories (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and types (preventive, deterring, detective, corrective, compensating, directive)
  • Change management: CAB, impact analysis, backout, maintenance window, documentation, version control
  • Cryptography: symmetric vs asymmetric, PKI, CSR, CRL vs OCSP, hash, salt, signature, key exchange, levels of encryption

2.0 Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks (24%)

  • CVE vs CVSS; threat feeds, likelihood and impact
  • Threat actors and motivations
  • Vectors: message, image, attachment, browser, network, remote, endpoint, supply chain, media, human, IoT, OT, physical, signal
  • Vulnerability types: unsupported, unpatched, zero-day, misconfiguration, hardcoded secrets, race conditions, shadow IT
  • Indicators: malware types, phishing family, DDoS, on-path, credential attacks, injection, IoCs
  • AI risks: poisoning, evasion, prompt injection, jailbreaking, hallucinations, data loss, bias, explainability

3.0 Security Architecture (19%)

  • Cloud, serverless, multicloud, IaC, OT, air gap, microservices, segmentation, data sovereignty
  • Zones and DMZ, device placement, fail open vs closed, Zero Trust, VPN, out-of-band, SSE
  • Data states, classification, masking, tokenization, hashing, data roles
  • Hot, warm, cold sites, redundancy, UPS and generator, backups (immutable), RTO, RPO, MTTR, MTBF

4.0 Security Operations (27%)

  • Hardening, allow lists, honeypot family, IDS vs IPS, WAF, UTM, EDR, XDR, DLP, NAC and 802.1X, SPF, DKIM, DMARC
  • Asset life cycle; vulnerability loop; CSPM, IPAM
  • SIEM, log aggregation, NetFlow, syslog, SNMP, SCAP, alert tuning
  • IAM: provisioning, federation (SAML, OAuth, LDAP), account types, MFA, access control models, JIT, passkeys
  • Automation vs orchestration, guardrails, agentic AI, CI/CD
  • Incident response phases, chain of custody, order of volatility, log and data sources

5.0 Program Management and Oversight (14%)

  • Policy, standard, procedure, guideline; AUP, BYOD, clean desk
  • Risk treatment (transfer, accept, avoid, mitigate); SLE × ARO = ALE; risk register; BIA
  • RFI, RFP, RFQ; SLA, MOU, MOA, NDA, MSA, SOW; right to audit
  • Compliance, privacy rights, legal hold
  • Audits, pen test types, passive vs active recon, MITRE ATT&CK
  • Awareness: initial, ongoing, targeted, corrective; BEC

4Pairs the exam likes to confuse

Pair Tell them apart
Detective vs corrective finds an incident vs fixes the damage
Deterring vs preventive discourages vs stops
Compensating vs corrective substitute for a missing control vs repair after the event
Virus vs worm vs Trojan needs a host vs spreads alone vs pretends to be useful
Spear phishing vs whaling targeted at a person or group vs at executives
Brute force vs spraying many passwords one account vs few passwords many accounts
IDS vs IPS alerts vs blocks
CRL vs OCSP list vs live query
Hashing vs encryption one way vs reversible
SAML vs OAuth authentication (SSO) vs delegated authorization
RTO vs RPO time down vs data lost
Poisoning vs evasion corrupt the training vs fool the trained model
MOU vs MOA non-binding vs binding
MSA vs SOW umbrella terms vs one project
Tokenization vs masking vault-backed substitute vs hidden display

5Common traps

  • A longer, more complex answer is not always better: pick the one that answers the question asked.
  • "FIRST" often means contain or verify, not eradicate or recover.
  • Encryption does not give integrity by itself; hashing does not give confidentiality.
  • Backups must be tested and immutable copies protect against ransomware.
  • Password plus PIN is not MFA (both are knowledge factors).
  • Insurance transfers risk; it does not remove it.
  • A self-signed certificate is not trusted by browsers.
  • A policy is mandatory; a guideline is optional.

6The final week

Day Do
7–5 One domain per day: read the cards and answer the recall questions from memory
4–3 The pairs table and the acronym list from the objectives, out loud
2 Redo all practice questions; list your misses and re-read those modules
1 Light review; check the test center or online rules and ID; rest

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Mixed practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors discovers that a workstation is sending data to an unknown server. What should the analyst do FIRST?

  • AReinstall the operating system
  • BDelete the logs
  • CReset all user passwords
  • DIsolate the workstation from the network
Show the answer

Answer: D. Containment comes first: isolating the host stops the spread and preserves evidence.

S2Which control best prevents a former employee's account from being used after they leave?

  • AA longer password policy
  • BA honeypot
  • CPort mirroring
  • DPrompt deprovisioning
Show the answer

Answer: D. Disabling or removing the account at departure prevents stale accounts from being abused.

S3A company must recover from a site failure within two hours and pay the lowest possible cost. Which site is the best compromise?

  • AWarm site
  • BCold site
  • CHot site
  • DNo recovery site
Show the answer

Answer: A. A warm site can restore in hours at a lower cost than a hot site.

S4Which action reduces the risk of ransomware destroying backups?

  • AImmutable backups
  • BMore frequent log reviews
  • CA second antivirus
  • DA larger firewall
Show the answer

Answer: A. Immutable backups cannot be altered or deleted for a set period.

S5An asset worth 200,000 has a 30% exposure factor and a loss is expected once every two years. What is the ALE?

  • A60,000
  • B100,000
  • C30,000
  • D120,000
Show the answer

Answer: C. SLE is 200,000 × 0.30 = 60,000 and ARO is 0.5, so ALE is 30,000 per year.

S6A user clicks a link in a text message and enters credentials on a fake page. Which attack and control pair is best?

  • AVishing and a firewall rule
  • BTailgating and a vestibule
  • CSmishing and security awareness training
  • DWhaling and SIEM tuning
Show the answer

Answer: C. A text-based phishing attack is smishing, addressed by awareness training and filtering.

S7Which standard lets an application access a user's data on another service without receiving the user's password?

  • ALDAP
  • BSAML for SSO
  • CRADIUS
  • DOAuth
Show the answer

Answer: D. OAuth provides delegated authorization using tokens.

S8A security team wants an early warning when someone browses to a fake finance folder. What should it use?

  • AA wildcard certificate
  • BA honeyfile
  • CA UPS
  • DA packet analyzer
Show the answer

Answer: B. A honeyfile is a decoy that alerts when it is opened.

S9A vendor contract should let the company check the vendor's controls at any time. Which clause is needed?

  • ALegal hold
  • BData transpose
  • CRight to audit
  • DClean desk
Show the answer

Answer: C. A right to audit clause allows inspection of the vendor's security.

S10A developer's code review finds an API key written in the source. Which fix is best?

  • AHash the key in the source
  • BAdd a comment to the code
  • CMove the secret to a managed vault and scan for secrets
  • DRename the file
Show the answer

Answer: C. Secrets should be stored in a vault, with scanning to prevent a repeat.

S11An executive receives an email that appears to come from the CFO asking for an urgent wire transfer. Which threat is this?

  • ACache poisoning
  • BLogic bomb
  • CBusiness email compromise
  • DRootkit
Show the answer

Answer: C. Impersonating an executive by email to move money is business email compromise.

S12A tester has the network diagrams and credentials before testing. Which test type is this?

  • AKnown environment
  • BUnknown environment
  • CPassive reconnaissance only
  • DPhysical
Show the answer

Answer: A. Having full information is a known environment (white box) test.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What is the passing score and scale?

Show the answer

750 on a scale of 100 to 900.

R2Which domain has the largest weight?

Show the answer

Security Operations (27%).

R3What do RTO and RPO measure?

Show the answer

The maximum downtime and the maximum data loss, in time.

R4What is the order of the risk treatments?

Show the answer

There is no order: transfer, accept, avoid and mitigate are four options.

R5What do you read first in a question?

Show the answer

The last sentence.

R6What is new in V8?

Show the answer

More coverage of AI-related risks, security operations and modern environments.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Time up to 90 questions, 90 minutes; quick questions first, PBQs next, flagged last; no blanks
Method last sentence, key words (BEST, FIRST, MOST), domain, remove wrong category, fit the constraint
Biggest confusions detective vs corrective, IDS vs IPS, SAML vs OAuth, RTO vs RPO, MOU vs MOA, MSA vs SOW, poisoning vs evasion
Traps "first" = contain, password plus PIN is not MFA, insurance transfers risk, test backups, self-signed is not trusted
